items.summary: A U.S. intelligence memo circulated earlier this year claimed that Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, according to multiple media reports led by The New York Times. A separate report alleged the two shared a romantic relationship. An Nvidia spokesperson said their interactions were "not unusual" and that the company does not share classified information with customers.
items.title: US intelligence memo reportedly links Megaspeed exec to spying on Nvidia chief

items.summary: The FAA announced that the first digital air traffic control towers are operational at Bartow executive airport (KBOW) in Florida and Kenai municipal airport (PAEN) in Alaska, with five more regional airports to follow. The systems give controllers a continuous 360-degree view of runways, taxiways and airspace through cameras and displays. The FAA says the technology supports rather than replaces human controllers as part of its $12.5bn modernization effort.
items.title: FAA Launches First Digital Air Traffic Control Towers in Florida and Alaska

items.summary: Zach and Scott of CleanTechnica picked up a new Tesla Model Y, which they call REDD, replacing an 180,000+ kilometre Model 3 named Tess. They describe the delivery centre as busy compared with seven years earlier when handovers took under three minutes in Brisbane. The author notes that in Australia the Model Y has been the highest selling passenger car of all drivetrains for recent months and even beat the refreshed Toyota RAV4 in October, while his own suburb is now full of them.
items.title: CleanTechnica editors trade their Model 3 for a new Tesla Model Y

items.summary: Tesla plans an extra production shift to finish outstanding Cybertruck orders before dismantling the line around June/July 2025, CEO Elon Musk said Saturday. The move follows his announcement that Texas Cybertruck output would wind down as resources shift toward the Cybercab robotaxi. US sales fell to about 20,000 vehicles in 2024 from nearly 39,000 in 2023, well below Musk's initial target of 250,000 annual sales.
items.title: Tesla Adds Shift to Clear Cybertruck Orders Before Line Closes for Cybercab

items.summary: Ipswich Town has opened a new Planet Blue store in Ipswich's Buttermarket shopping centre, the club says, describing it as a commitment to fans and the town. Captain Dara O'Shea cut the ribbon on Friday, saying the club is 'the heart of the town.' The opening coincided with the release of the club's black and gold third kit.
items.title: Ipswich Town opens town-centre club shop

items.summary: New Zealand elected a new government on Saturday as fog blanketed Wellington, even though voters expressed widespread apathy and disillusionment. Polling suggests low national mood with faith in politics lower still; more than half no longer see the country as a land of opportunity. A record number deserted the two major parties, giving neither a clear mandate, while smaller parties gained ground. Unemployment sits at an 11-year high, youth job prospects are poor, and household electricity bills have jumped sharply. About 180 people left the country daily in a record exodus. Former prime minister Helen Clark says New Zealand faces a crisis of confidence about its identity and direction.
items.title: New Zealand's New Government Faces Disillusioned Voters Amid Economic Hardship

items.summary: Ueno Bank, a digital lender that expanded quickly after being allowed to become a bank under President Santiago Peña’s government, was ordered into resolution by the central bank on Monday night over insolvency. Overnight it froze accounts for nearly 3 million Paraguayans, about 60% of adults, and left roughly 32,000 pensioners without payments. The crisis led congress to impeach and place Peña under house arrest; prosecutors charged him with breach of trust and requested preventive custody, though he denies the allegations. An estimated $800m to $860m in state and pension funds were invested in Ueno. A guarantee fund is paying customers up to $1,565 who meet three requirements, but most affected people still cannot access their money as protests grow.
items.title: Paraguay Bank Collapse Topples President and Freezes Millions in Accounts

items.summary: The ninth China International Import Expo runs from November 5 to November 10, 2023, in Shanghai under the theme "Equipping Tomorrow Together." Its Intelligent Industry & Information Technology Exhibition Area covers five major sections: digital industrial automation, integrated circuits, low-carbon energy and environmental technologies, artificial intelligence (AI), and new materials. Booths feature products from KraussMaffei, Intel, Brother, Henkel, SINDAN, Honeywell, Samsung Electronics, Tesla, Heraeus Group, Iron Horse Quantum Laboratory, Schneider Electric, and Hitch Open.
items.title: CIIE Opens in Shanghai With Focus on Industrial Innovation

items.summary: President Isaac Herzog has tapped Gadi Eisenkot to form the next Israeli government instead of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Although Likud won the most seats with 27, neither party secured a majority in Israel's 120-seat parliament. Eisenkot now has up to six weeks to negotiate and win the 61 seats needed for a majority.
items.title: Israel's President Appoints Eisenkot, Not Netanyahu, To Form Government

items.summary: Kumar Balasingam, a Singapore collector and CEO of JSD Group, founded in 1996, has spent decades building a classic car collection. He bought his first 1972 Alfa Romeo 2000 GTV at 19 using S$12,000 borrowed from his mother. His collection eventually grew to about 45 vehicles, mostly Alfa Romeos with some Ferraris and Aston Martins. After selling the original GTV in 2000 due to a COE renewal cost of over S$40,000, he rediscovered it three years later at a workshop in Melaka. He now restores cars across Italy, Poland, Hungary, Malaysia, and the United States.
items.title: Singapore Collector's Lifelong Alfa Romeo Passion

items.summary: Richard Lloyd, founding member and guitarist of the punk band Television, has died at age 75. His family confirmed he passed away Saturday morning in Chattanooga, Tennessee, with his wife Sheila and dog Willie Mays beside him. He had been diagnosed with cholangiocarcinoma in March 2026. Television formed in 1973 and its debut album Marquee Moon was ranked No 107 on Rolling Stone's 2023 list of the 500 greatest albums.
items.title: Television guitarist Richard Lloyd dies aged 75

items.summary: Chinese scientists aboard China's space station created what they describe as the coldest known artificial matter, cooling a cloud of rubidium atoms to an equivalent temperature of just 9.7 picokelvins using the ultracold atom physics facility in the Mengtian lab module. The team observed the cloud's expansion for seven seconds and published the findings in Science on November 6.
items.title: Chinese Scientists Set Record With Coldest Artificial Matter in Space

items.summary: Fifty years after its first documented outbreak in what is now the Democratic Republic of Congo, a less common Bundibugyo type of Orthoebolavirus has triggered another major Ebola outbreak. Experts from Germany's DZIF argue that decades of prior exposure to the virus meant vaccines and treatments could have been developed earlier but were not pursued. Although Ervebo is already licensed for the Zaire variant, no approved protection exists against Bundibugyo or other strains. A recent study found cross-reactive immune responses in lab tests, though it cannot yet confirm real-world protection. Researchers warn that mass vaccination without proof of efficacy could undermine trust and complicate future trials; practical containment remains hampered by conflict and transport challenges. Experts estimate a usable vaccine may not arrive until mid-2027.
items.title: Why No Ebola Vaccine Exists Despite Decades of Knowledge

items.summary: Artist Ryhia Dank illustrated a collection of $1 and $2 'Our Animals, Our Country' coins showing native animals with their names in the Gudanji/Wakaja language. The project was released this week through a collaboration between the Australian Mint, Australia Post and the Indigenous Literacy Foundation (ILF). Dank hopes children will recognise traditional animals like crocodiles and brolgas on currency to keep First Nations languages alive. Experts say visibility strengthens revitalisation: First Languages Australia noted fewer than 100 of more than 700 documented languages are used daily, while University of Queensland professor Felicity Meakins said 'You can't be what you can't see.' ILF chief executive Ben Bowen called the coins a way to spark curiosity and start conversations about language. Dank is an ILF ambassador; the foundation has donated more than 150,000 books to approximately 508 communities over almost 20 years.
items.title: Indigenous artist designs animal-named coins for language revival

items.summary: Swimmer Moesha Johnson won gold in both the 10km and 3km elimination races at the opening leg of the 2026 Open Water World Cup, held in Cancún. She had already taken every race last year's edition plus the Pan Pacs event in California. The next stage is scheduled for Somabay, Egypt on March 19 and 20, 2027.
items.title: Moesha Johnson Wins Double Gold at Open Water World Cup Opener in Cancún

items.summary: Ukraine's emergency services released footage showing firefighters battling flames at industrial structures hit by Russian strikes in the Kyiv region. The attacks also damaged energy facilities and a major bridge, leaving a kindergarten severely injured with scattered rubble and toys. Five people were reported wounded. As Ukraine prepares for winter amid ongoing bombardment of its strained power network, diplomatic talks between Ukraine, Russia and the United States continue.
items.title: Russian Strikes Damage Kyiv Region Infrastructure and Kindergarten

items.summary: Liverpool Football Club says it is taking action against online retailers selling unauthorised football shirts that carry pro-Palestinian slogans alongside a modified version of the club crest. The organisation UK Lawyers for Israel alerted four Premier League clubs to possible trade mark infringements on 26 October 2026, and Jewish News reported the matter on 5 November. Liverpool FC says fans could mistake these shirts for official merchandise and wrongly attribute political support to the club; it has referred sales offers to website operators and social networks over possible trademark breaches under the Trade Marks Act 1994 and plans further action.
items.title: Liverpool FC Takes Action Over Counterfeit Pro-Palestinian Shirts

items.summary: Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee staged a protest outside her nephew Abhishek Banerjee's residence in the Kalighat area of south Kolkata, alleging that his home had been targeted in a pre-planned attack during a Kali Puja celebration. She accused the BJP and police of intimidating political opponents and said she might approach the Supreme Court over lawlessness in the state. Later, after a confrontation between police and Trinamool supporters, Abhishek Banerjee claimed the attack continued until 7 am and cited crime figures for May to October. He also alleged it was the seventh attempt on his life in six months.
items.title: Mamata Banerjee protests alleged attack on Abhishek's home in Kolkata

items.summary: A gunman killed six people in Krakow’s Old Town on Saturday before being injured in a shootout with police near the Main Market Square. Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski said he is likely a domestic far-right extremist and quoted himself saying “Everything indicates he was fascinated by far-right ideology. ” Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz called it terrorism, while Prime Minister Donald Tusk and President Karol Nawrocki urged full explanations. Four women and two men died; 16 others were hurt, including three officers. The suspect’s identity remains unpublicized. Krakow is a Unesco World Heritage Site of about 800,000 people roughly 250 km (150 miles) south of Warsaw.
items.title: Krakow Shooting Kills Six, Suspect Tied to Far-Right Ideology
